Following the launch of teacher-led Gemini Notebook in Google Classroom, we are introducing insight summaries for educators. This update provides teachers with greater visibility into how students interact with assigned notebooks, helping gauge instructional value and inform lesson planning.
Teachers now have access to actionable insight summaries, powered by Gemini, based on student conversations with teacher-assigned notebooks. Teachers can see:


An overall summary of how students engaged with the assigned notebook
A sample of common themes to help inform instruction, such as common questions, areas of strength and suggested areas to support.
Individual student chat transcripts for assigned notebooks for additional context and to confirm the accuracy of AI provided insights.





This functionality is only available for Gemini Notebooks assigned through Google Classroom, and students will see a notification in the assigned notebook informing them that their conversations in their assigned notebook are visible to their teacher.
Additionally, Google Workspace administrators can now enable external sharing for Gemini Notebook using granular controls in the Admin console, including Trusted Domains. For example, this now allows Classroom users to create and assign notebooks if teachers and students are in different domains that are designated as trusted domains, if sharing with trusted domains is enabled by admins.

# Google Classroom's AI Notebook Now Summarizes How Students Use It

> **In short:** Google is rolling out Gemini-powered insight summaries for teachers in Classroom, showing how students engaged with assigned notebooks. Teachers can also see common themes and individual chat transcripts, alongside new admin controls for cross-school sharing.

If you've ever handed out an assignment and wondered whether the class actually read the instructions, this update is aimed at teachers. Google says it is adding insight summaries to its teacher-led Gemini Notebook in Classroom — a way to look back, after the fact, at how students actually used an AI workspace you assigned them.

## What's new for teachers

The update builds on the teacher-led Gemini Notebook, which lets teachers hand out guided AI notebooks (think of them as small, focused AI workspaces attached to a lesson) to students. Until now, a teacher could assign the work but had very little visibility into what happened inside the chat.

According to Google's announcement, the new insight summaries — powered by Gemini (Google's AI model, the engine behind the Gemini chatbot) — give teachers three views in one place:

- **An overall engagement summary** of how the class used the assigned notebook
- **Common themes** — recurring questions, things students understood well, and spots where the class seemed to struggle
- **Individual student chat transcripts** for the assigned notebook, so the teacher can double-check what the AI summarized

One small but important detail: Google says students will see a notification inside the assigned notebook telling them their conversations are visible to their teacher. Nothing here is hidden.

## A new option for school admins

The second piece is for the people running the school's Google Workspace — the IT staff and admins who decide who can share what. Google says admins can now turn on external sharing for Gemini Notebooks through finer controls in the Admin console, including a "Trusted Domains" option.

In plain terms: if a teacher and their students sit in different school domains — for example, a teacher at one school working with students from a partner school — admins can now let those notebooks be shared across those trusted domains, where that sharing is turned on.

## What this means for you

- **If you're a teacher**: You'll get a much faster read on whether an assignment landed. Instead of reading every conversation, you see themes — and you can spot-check the transcripts when something looks off. The trade-off is that you'll want to design your prompts carefully: open-ended tasks tend to produce richer insights than very narrow ones.
- **If you're a student (or a parent)**: Your teacher can now see your conversations inside assigned notebooks. Google says you'll get a notification, so there are no surprises. Treat the chat like a classroom conversation — useful for learning, but not private.
- **If you're a school or district admin**: Check the Admin console for the new Trusted Domains toggle. If your schools already partner on cross-classroom projects, you'll likely want to enable this deliberately rather than leave it off.
- **If you already use Google Classroom heavily**: Pair the new insight summaries with your existing rubrics (the scoring guides you grade work against). The summaries are most useful as a starting point for a class conversation, not as a stand-alone grade.

## Wrap-up

Google's Classroom update turns the teacher-led Notebook from a black box into something a teacher can actually inspect. The summaries save time, the transcripts keep the AI honest, and the new admin controls make the feature usable across schools that trust each other. If you teach with Classroom, your next step is to assign a notebook and check the insights after your students have worked through it — the data only appears once they've actually used it.
